newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Austrim will not raise Hawker bid again.
newsitem.headline: Austrim will not raise Hawker bid again.

text.p: Manufacturing and investment group Austrim Ltd said on Wednesday it would not increase again its takeover bid price for auto parts group Hawker Richardson Ltd and the bid would not be extended beyond August 7.
"In coming to this conclusion, the board of Austrim concluded that the offer price of $1.86 for each share is a full and fair price for the Hawker shares," Austrim said.
It said it noted all of Hawker's directors unanimously recommended Austrim's offer of $1.86 per share be accepted.

Austrim said the offer price represented a premium of about 40 percent on the pre-announcement trading price of A$1.34, "being in excess of the average control premium in recent comparable transactions."
The offer price was also about four times Hawker's net tangible assets, which was well above the premiums received in recent comparable takeovers, Austrim said.
Austrim agreed on June 30 to raise its bid price to A$1.86 a share from its initial bid price of A$1.60, which secured the recommendation to accept from Austrim's board.
But several large pension fund shareholders have refused to accept the bid.
Austrim's last substantial shareholder notice showed it had secured acceptances for 14.99 million or 40.9 percent of Hawker shares.
Hawker's shares were down one cent at A$1.86 by 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), while Austrim was up one cent at A$4.58.
